transcript:
Agent: Thank you for calling card customer support. My name is Marcus. How can I help you today?
Customer: Hi Marcus, I'm calling because there's a charge on my account that I really don't think I should have to pay for.
Agent: I can help look into that with you. May I have your full name and the billing zip code on the account?
Customer: Sure, it's Dmitri Sorensen, and my zip code is 97201.
Agent: Thank you, Mr. Sorensen. Which transaction are you calling about?
Customer: It's from a restaurant called The Gilded Fork for $76.40, from September 30th.
Agent: I see that transaction here on September 30th for $76.40. Can you tell me a little more about what happened?
Customer: Well, my friend and I went in for dinner, and honestly, the whole experience was just awful. The food was practically inedible.
Agent: I'm sorry to hear your meal wasn't good. Did you speak with anyone at the restaurant about the issue?
Customer: We mentioned to the server that the meat was super dry and cold, but they seemed busy and just kind of brushed it off. We didn't want to cause a scene or argue, so when the check came, I just gave them my card and signed it.
Agent: Did you end up eating the food while you were there?
Customer: We ate most of it because we'd been waiting for an hour and were starving, but it was really poor quality.
Agent: Have you contacted the restaurant or spoken with a manager since you left that evening?
Customer: No, I haven't reached out to them since. I figured I would just call you guys directly to get the charge removed.
Agent: So to make sure I have the details straight, you ate at The Gilded Fork on September 30th, paid the $76.40 at the end of the meal, and you're requesting to have the charge taken off your card because the food quality was unacceptable.
Customer: Yes, exactly. I just don't think I should be paying for a dinner that bad.
